messages:
caroline_cs: Heads-up — ACME reported the console hourly usage missing between 00:00-06:00 local time after midnight. They see last entry at 23:00 then jump to 07:00. tenant_id=acme-42. Noticed in dashboard and raw queries. @jamie_data can you triage?

jamie_data: On it. Quick question: do they override timezone in the tenant settings? My suspicion is an ETL partitioning key issue.

caroline_cs: They use America/Los_Angeles. Dashboard currently groups by UTC hour which they understand, but they expect consecutive local hours. They say this started after last night's deploy.

jamie_data: I repro'd on staging by replaying the ingest. Hourly_rollups query shows gaps. Example SQL I ran: 
```sql
SELECT hour_bucket, count(*)
FROM hourly_rollups
WHERE tenant_id='acme-42' AND hour_bucket >= '2026-03-15'
GROUP BY hour_bucket
ORDER BY hour_bucket;
```
Results jump 2026-03-15T23:00Z -> 2026-03-16T07:00Z (gap ~8 rows).

li_sre: Any errors in the nightly ETL logs? @ingest-bot can you paste the partitioner logs from the 00:00-08:00 window?

ingest-bot: deploy:etl-runner v3.2.1 started 1912345600, finished 1912349200. No fatal exit errors. Warnings present: "timezone conversion deprecated in utils/ptime.py line 88".

jamie_data: Found the culprit in recent commit 8f3a: we switched to using `local_time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H')` when building hour buckets instead of normalizing to UTC first. On hosts where TZ env var is set to America/Los_Angeles this shifts the bucket backwards. Sample log: 
```
WARN partitioner: using local tz for hour buckets: tz=America/Los_Angeles offset=-07:00
```

li_sre: :facepalm: That would create a 7-8 hour offset gap for tenants expecting UTC grouping. Plan: hotfix partitioner to use UTC-normalized times, run per-tenant backfills for affected windows.

jamie_data: Will open PR now to revert and add explicit timezone normalization. Patch excerpt: 
```diff
- bucket = local_time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H')
+ utc_time = local_time.astimezone(pytz.UTC).replace(tzinfo=None)
+ bucket = utc_time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H')
```
Canary then full rollout. Also adding unit/regression tests.

caroline_cs: Customer asks if we can manually backfill their missing hours and ETA to repopulate console.

jamie_data: Yes. We can rerun hourly ingestion for acme-42 for the missing window. Backfill command: `./scripts/backfill_hourly.sh --tenant acme-42 --start 2026-03-15T00:00Z --end 2026-03-15T06:00Z`. Expected runtime ~10-20m depending on rows.

li_sre: Approving canary deploy. @maya_support please tell the customer: hotfix + targeted backfill scheduled in ~30-45m, metrics should appear within 10-15m after backfill completes.

maya_support: Messaging drafted: "Sorry about the missing hours — root cause was a timezone handling bug introduced in last night's deploy. We will hotfix and run a backfill for your tenant (acme-42). ETA 45 minutes, I'll DM when done." :thumbsup:

jamie_data: Backfill started; tail of logs: 
```
INFO backfill: tenant=acme-42 window=2026-03-15T00:00Z-2026-03-15T06:00Z rows_scanned=0->1256 rows_written=0->1256
```

ingest-bot: Canary deploy of v3.2.2 (partitioner fix) successful on two nodes; no exception traces. Starting full rollout.

jamie_data: Full rollout complete. Regression test added for timezone normalization. Backfill finished and hourly_rollups now include 00:00-06:00.

caroline_cs: Customer confirmed they see the previously missing hours populated in the console. They requested a postmortem. Assign jamie_data + li_sre please.

li_sre: I'll write the postmortem. Draft will include: root cause (local-time bucketization introduced in commit 8f3a), timeline, remediation (hotfix + backfill), and action items: stricter review for datetime handling, add monitoring alert for hourly gaps >1h, and an automated per-tenant backfill runbook.

maya_support: Closing the loop with the customer and internal docs updated. :white_check_mark:
